title: A contact binds two processes exactly when it is a parity of two remembering contact cells
subject: Which contacts between two processes, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law, bind both
conclusion: Two rings, each running an elementary cellular automaton, and one contact cell that reads one cell of each and feeds nothing back, written as one space-time law. The contact binds both rings at lag T, every minimally decisive set of its value c(T) meeting both, exactly when neither ring's first row with the contact's own first value decides c(T), which is also exactly when forgetting either ring leaves c(T) free: the contact gate's two-sided essentiality and loss under erasure, read across time. The contact sees each ring only through the histories that ring can show at its contact cell. A memoryless contact binds exactly when it is XOR or XNOR of two contact cells that still depend on their first rows, its knots joining one decisive set of each ring, and a contact with memory binds at lag 1 exactly when it is one of the four parities. Between linear rings the parity contact binds at every lag exactly when neither ring polynomial is nilpotent modulo X^m - 1, which fails only for rules 0 and 255, and for 60, 102 and 90 and their negations on rings of 2^k cells.
